mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite a statistically significant positive correlation (p < 0.05) between the labor indicators and the return in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months reduces policy uncertainty and prompts risk-on positioning, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns remain negative even when controlling for other macro variables (FEDFUNDS, UNRATE) in a multivariate regression (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in manufacturing employment (implied via PAYEMS) indicates weakening supply capacity, which can lead to temporary S&P 500 forward returns of -1% over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 2% month-over-month and PAYEMS shows a downward trend for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly different from the prior month's average (p > 0.1 in rolling t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, the discount rate applied to future earnings is expected to rise, reducing the present value of equity prospects and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Over 60 days following the trigger, the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than during periods of similar FEDFUNDS levels (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in weekly job openings (implied via PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment suggests a tight labor market, which can boost investor sentiment and drive S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS shows an abrupt monthly increase of > 10% from the prior month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite a significant positive single-variable regression coefficient (p < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% create expectations of lower future policy rates, which can support equity valuations and produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 60-day 20-day forward return average is not statistically higher than during periods of rising inflation (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-constrained environment characterized by a sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a sharp drop in consumer confidence (implied via HOUST) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 3% month-over-month and HOUST falls by > 15 points in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly negative in a multivariate regression that includes lagged supply and sentiment variables (p > 0.1).
